title: EMI, interest rates — flat vs reducing balance
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is a fixed payment that covers part principal and part interest. On a 'reducing balance' loan, interest is charged only on what you still owe, so the interest part of each EMI shrinks over time — banks and most regulated lenders quote this. On a 'flat rate' loan, interest is charged on the original amount for the whole tenure, so the real cost is much higher: a 10% flat rate is roughly equal to a 17–19% reducing rate. Always compare loans using the APR / effective annual rate and the total repayment, not the monthly EMI alone. A longer tenure lowers the EMI but raises total interest. Check for processing fees, prepayment or foreclosure charges, and read the Key Fact Statement the lender must give you. A safe guideline is to keep all EMIs together below about 40% of your monthly take-home income.
summary_hinglish: EMI mein principal aur interest dono hote hain. Reducing balance mein byaj bachi hui raqam par lagta hai; flat rate mein poori original raqam par, isliye flat 10% lagbhag 17-19% reducing ke barabar hota hai. Loan compare karte waqt APR aur total repayment dekho, sirf EMI nahi. Saari EMIs milakar income ke 40% se kam rakho.
summary_hi: EMI में मूलधन और ब्याज दोनों होते हैं। रिड्यूसिंग बैलेंस में ब्याज बकाया रकम पर लगता है, फ्लैट रेट में मूल रकम पर पूरे समय, इसलिए फ्लैट 10% लगभग 17-19% रिड्यूसिंग के बराबर होता है। लोन तुलना में APR और कुल भुगतान देखें, सारी EMI आय के 40% से कम रखें।
